author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (concept and Meshy generation), brought inside its budget in-repo by the project's headless Blender pipeline
tool: Meshy (image-to-3D), run by the maintainer OUTSIDE this repository and delivered already texture-optimised -- which reduces the maps, not the mesh, so it still arrived at 1,972,184 triangles. Reduced inside the repository by tools/decimate_model.py (headless Blender 4.0.2): the Draco-compressed export was decoded, coincident vertices welded, the mesh collapse-decimated to 10,000, the three 2048 maps kept at their source resolution -- the texture ceiling is applied by halving, and they already sat on it, and the result gated on two-way surface deviation and on open edges. The maps were renamed by the Principled BSDF input each one feeds, so Godot's extracted textures land on contract-conforming names.
prompt: Generated by the maintainer in Meshy; the exact Meshy prompt is theirs and is not recorded in this repository. The dense source is kept at reference/coral_cove/Netgrin_Salvage_Bot.glb so the reduction can be re-run at any ratio. SUPERSEDES the procedurally generated Netbot from tools/blender/make_drift_fleet.py, whose provenance described it as 'a squat entangling machine: a cube body with four splayed casting arms over a slung net plate, with an amber lamp on top'; that generator remains in the repository and still produces a valid prop. Shipped at the prop category's 10,000-triangle budget, and this unit is why that budget is not negotiable for the fleet: it is the densest-detailed of the three and the one that strays furthest under reduction. At 5,000 its net strayed 3.07% of the bounding-box diagonal and the deviation gate refused the file outright -- exactly the failure that gate exists to catch, since the triangle count alone would have called it a success. At 10,000 it measures 1.34%. Checked by render at the shipped count: the red and teal body and the slung net read as the machine that entangles.
licenseTerms: Meshy's terms of service govern the generated mesh and its maps; the maintainer generated the asset under their own Meshy account and contributed it to this repository. The in-repo Blender pass that reduces it is Apache-2.0 with the rest of the project, but it does not change the terms on the geometry it transforms. REVIEW NEEDED (REQ-021) before any redistribution that assumes a uniform Apache-2.0 grant over assets/, and it is sharper for this asset than for the hero: the project's promise to contributors is 'build your level out of our assets', which is a grant that cannot be made over geometry whose terms are someone else's.
